title: Morphisms into a disjoint union of copies of the base are clopen decompositions
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ a set. Let $U_E=\coprod_{e\in E}U$ be the coproduct of copies of $U$ indexed by $E$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with coprojections $\iota_e:U\to U_E$, and let $\pi:U_E\to U$ be the morphism with $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_U$ for all $e\in E$; write $V_e=\iota_e(U)\subseteq U_E$. Let $s:W\to U$ be a morphism of schemes. Call a family $(W_e)_{e\in E}$ of open subsets of $W$ an *$E$-indexed clopen decomposition* of $W$ if the $W_e$ are pairwise disjoint and $W=\bigcup_{e\in E}W_e$ (then each $W_e$ is also closed); regard each $W_e$ as an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] with inclusion $j_e:W_e\to W$. Then: (a) for every morphism $f:W\to U_E$ with $\pi\circ f=s$, the family $(f^{-1}(V_e))_{e\in E}$ is an $E$-indexed clopen decomposition of $W$, and $f\circ j_e=\iota_e\circ s\circ j_e$ on $W_e=f^{-1}(V_e)$ for every $e\in E$; (b) for every $E$-indexed clopen decomposition $(W_e)_{e\in E}$ of $W$ there is exactly one morphism $f:W\to U_E$ with $\pi\circ f=s$ and $f^{-1}(V_e)=W_e$ for all $e\in E$. Hence $f\mapsto(f^{-1}(V_e))_{e\in E}$ is a bijection from the set of $U$-morphisms $W\to U_E$ onto the set of $E$-indexed clopen decompositions of $W$, equivalently onto the set of maps $\varphi:|W|\to E$ all of whose fibres are open ($W_e=\varphi^{-1}(e)$). (c) For $e_0\in E$ the morphism $\iota_{e_0}\circ s$ corresponds to the decomposition with $W_{e_0}=W$ and $W_e=\varnothing$ for $e\neq e_0$ (the constant map with value $e_0$). For $E=\varnothing$, $U_\varnothing$ is the empty scheme, and a $U$-morphism $W\to U_\varnothing$ exists (and is then unique) if and only if $W$ is empty.

proof.text: Step 3. For a disjoint covering P of W, Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Limits.nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of identifies the cofan of its open inclusions as a coproduct. This is the disjoint gluing mapping property of 01JB, also found in the searches of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Descend the maps (P e).ι ≫ s ≫ Sigma.ι G e through this colimit. Its fac equations give the restrictions. At a point x choose a covering piece e′. sigmaι_eq_iff shows that its image belongs to component e precisely when e = e′; disjointness of P gives the same criterion for x ∈ P e. Hence the preimage family is P. Colimit hom_ext gives the equation over U and uniqueness using the forced restriction equation of Step 2.

proof.text: Step 4. The inverse-image map from morphisms over U to decompositions is injective by the uniqueness of Step 3 and surjective by its existence. Equiv.ofBijective gives the first equivalence. Map a locally constant function to its open fibres. This map is injective pointwise. For a decomposition, choose the unique piece containing each point; disjointness proves that its fibres are exactly the prescribed pieces. IsLocallyConstant.iff_isOpen_fiber proves local constancy. The fibre map is thus bijective. Compose the first equivalence with its inverse, and use apply_symm_apply to prove the stated fibre equation.

proof.text: Step 5. For s ≫ Sigma.ι G e₀, sigmaι_eq_iff proves that component e has preimage top when e = e₀ and bottom otherwise. For empty E, sigmaOpenCover.exists_eq would produce an impossible index at any point of the coproduct, so it is empty. A morphism to this empty scheme makes W empty. Conversely isInitialOfIsEmpty constructs the morphism from empty W; its hom_ext proves the equation over U.
